arxiv-1408-1110.title: Modeling Basic Aspects of Cyber-Physical Systems, Part II
arxiv-1408-1110.creator: Yingfu Zeng, Chad Rose, Paul Brauner, Walid Taha, Jawad Masood, Roland Philippsen, Marcia O’Malley, Robert Cartwright
arxiv-1408-1110.description: Abstract We continue to consider the question of what language features are needed to effectively model cyber-physical systems (CPS). In previous work, we proposed using a core language as a way to study this question, and showed how several basic aspects of CPS can be modeled clearly in a language with a small set of constructs.

arxiv-2202-12249.title: Illuminating the nucleon spin
arxiv-2202-12249.creator: Miguel G. Echevarria
arxiv-2202-12249.description: Abstract In this short note the QED extension of the nucleon spin sum rule is considered. To this end, the leading-order (LO) QED evolution kernels for the quark/gluon helicity and orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distributions are calculated, as well as their lepton and photon analogue distributions introduced for the first time.

arxiv-2204-06725.title: Monadicity of Non-deterministic Logical Matrices is Undecidable
arxiv-2204-06725.creator: Pedro Filipe Carlos Caleiro Sérgio Marcelino
arxiv-2204-06725.description: Abstract The notion of non-deterministic logical matrix (where connectives are interpreted as multi-functions) preserves many good properties of traditional semantics based on logical matrices (where connectives are interpreted as functions) whilst finitely characterizing a much wider class of logics, and has proven to be decisive in a myriad of recent compositional results in logic.

arxiv-2206-02697.title: Convergence and local-to-global results for p p\mspace{1mu} -superminimizers on quasiopen sets
arxiv-2206-02697.creator: Anders Björn
arxiv-2206-02697.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, several convergence results for fine p\mspace{1mu} -(super)minimizers on quasiopen sets in metric spaces are obtained. For this purpose, we deduce a Caccioppoli-type inequality and local-to-global principles for fine p\mspace{1mu} -(super)minimizers on quasiopen sets. A substantial part of these considerations is to show that the functions belong to a suitable local fine Sobolev space.

arxiv-2206-06532.title: On a Mathematical Model of the Rotating Atmosphere of the Earth
arxiv-2206-06532.creator: Tetu Makino
arxiv-2206-06532.description: Abstract In meteorology the analysis of motions of the atmosphere on the Earth has been done using various mathematical models and using various approximations. In this article as the simplest model the compressible Euler equations with barotropic equation of state of the ideal gas is analyzed under the co-ordinate system which rotates with constant angular velocity.

arxiv-2206-07584.title: Scattering of light waves from a collection with particles of ℒ \mathcal{L} types
arxiv-2206-07584.creator: Yi Ding
arxiv-2206-07584.description: Abstract A new approach is developed within the first-order Born approximation to light scattering from a collection of particles with ℒ \mathcal{L} types. Two ℒ × ℒ \mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{L} matrices called pair-potential matrix (PPM) and pair-structure matrix (PSM) are introduced to jointly formulate the coherence properties of the scattered field.

arxiv-2310-03575.title: Analysis of Learning a Flow-based Generative Model from Limited Sample Complexity
arxiv-2310-03575.creator: Hugo Cui, Florent Krzakala, Eric Vanden-Eijnden, Lenka Zdeborová
arxiv-2310-03575.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hugo Cui, Florent Krzakala, Eric Vanden-Eijnden, Lenka Zdeborová. We study the problem of training a flow-based generative model, parametrized by a two-layer autoencoder, to sample from a high-dimensional Gaussian mixture. We provide a sharp end-to-end analysis of the problem. First, we provide a tight closed-form characterization of the learnt velocity field, when parametrized by a shallow denoising auto-encoder trained on a finite number n n of samples from the target distribution.

arxiv-2401-10291.title: Detecting Post-Stroke Aphasia Via Brain Responses to Speech in a Deep Learning Framework
arxiv-2401-10291.creator: Pieter De Clercq 1 1 , Corentin Puffay 1 1, 2 , Jill Kries 1 , Hugo Van Hamme 2 , Maaike Vandermosten 1 , Tom Francart 1 and Jonas Vanthornhout 1
arxiv-2401-10291.description: Abstract Aphasia, a language disorder primarily caused by a stroke, is traditionally diagnosed using behavioral language tests. However, these tests are time-consuming, require manual interpretation by trained clinicians, suffer from low ecological validity, and diagnosis can be biased by comorbid motor and cognitive problems present in aphasia.

arxiv-2404-12627.title: A Soft e-Textile Sensor for Enhanced Deep Learning-based Shape Sensing of Soft Continuum Robots
arxiv-2404-12627.creator: Eric Vincent Galeta, Ayman A. Nada, Sabah M. Ahmed, Victor Parque, Haitham El-Hussieny
arxiv-2404-12627.description: Abstract The safety and accuracy of robotic navigation hold paramount importance, especially in the realm of soft continuum robotics, where the limitations of traditional rigid sensors become evident. Encoders, piezoresistive, and potentiometer sensors often fail to integrate well with the flexible nature of these robots, adding unwanted bulk and rigidity.

arxiv-2407-08999.title: Acoustic Analogue for Quantum Field Theory with a Source term
arxiv-2407-08999.creator: Akshat Pandey
arxiv-2407-08999.description: Abstract We propose a non-relativistic fluid analogue model for a scalar field coupled to a classical source. The generic analogue gravity model involves the phonon-field which is coupled to the acoustic metric. We work in the special relativity limit of the acoustic analogue.

arxiv-2502-03011.title: Multiband Nonthermal Radiative Properties of the Pulsar Wind Nebula CTB 87
arxiv-2502-03011.creator: Yunlu Gong, Liancheng Zhou, Qi Xia, Haiyun Zhang, Jun Fang, Li Zhang
arxiv-2502-03011.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yunlu Gong, Liancheng Zhou, Qi Xia, Haiyun Zhang, Jun Fang, Li Zhang. The pulsar wind nebula CTB 87 (G74.9+1.2) is one of the sources emitting γ \gamma -rays with energies higher than 10 TeV, as measured by the Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System telescope (VERITAS). In this study, we undertake a reanalysis of the GeV emission from the CTB 87 region, utilising ∼ \sim 16 years of high-energy γ \gamma -ray data collected with the Fermi Large Area Telescope.

arxiv-2503-03753.title: Generative Diffusion Model-based Compression of MIMO CSI
arxiv-2503-03753.creator: Heasung Kim, Taekyun Lee, Hyeji Kim, Gustavo De Veciana, Mohamed Amine Arfaoui, Asil Koc, Phil Pietraski, Guodong Zhang, John Kaewell
arxiv-2503-03753.description: Abstract While neural lossy compression techniques have markedly advanced the efficiency of Channel State Information (CSI) compression and reconstruction for feedback in MIMO communications, efficient algorithms for more challenging and practical tasks—such as CSI compression for future channel prediction and reconstruction with relevant side information—remain underexplored, often resulting in suboptimal performance when existing methods are extended to these scenarios.

arxiv-2503-22598.title: Integrable Corners in the Space of Gukov-Witten Surface Defects
arxiv-2503-22598.creator: Adam Chalabi, Charlotte Kristjansen, Chenliang Su
arxiv-2503-22598.description: Abstract We investigate integrability properties of Gukov-Witten 1/2-BPS surface defects in S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory in the large- N N limit. We demonstrate that ordinary Gukov-Witten defects, which depend on a set of continuous parameters, are not integrable except for special sub-sectors.

pmc-10608947.title: Efficient Mineralization of Fluoroelastomers Using Superheated Water in the Presence of Potassium Hydroxide
pmc-10608947.creator: Jin Hamaura, Hisao Hori, Ayane Fujishima, Hirofumi Mukae
pmc-10608947.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The mineralization of fluoroelastomers (FKMs) in superheated water in the presence of potassium hydroxide (KOH) was investigated with the aim of developing a methodology for recycling the fluorine element. Two FKMs—an “uncrosslinked FKM”, representing a poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (poly(VDF-co-HFP)) copolymer with a VDF/HFP molar ratio of 78/22 and a “crosslinked FKM” consisting of this copolymer (cured by peroxide) and carbon black—were treated.

pmc-10644028.creator: Angel M Carcaboso
pmc-10644028.description: the erythroblast transformation-specific (ETS) transcription factor family, usually (85%) Friend leukemia virus integration 1 proto-oncogene (FLI1; fusion EWSR1-FLI1) and less commonly (10%) ETS-related gene (ERG; fusion EWSR1-ERG) (2). At diagnosis, around 20–30% of patients with Ewing sarcoma have metastases, which indicates the presence of a high-risk disease.

pmc-10672902.title: Comorbidities and Laryngeal Cancer in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Review
pmc-10672902.creator: Beata Kiss, Cristian Mircea Neagos, Gabriela Jimborean, Hédi Katalin Sárközi, Mioara Szathmary, Adriana Neagos
pmc-10672902.description: Introductions: The global prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea shows that this disease appears in 1 billion people, with the prevalence exceeding 50% in some countries. Treatment is necessary to minimize negative health impacts. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is defined as a cause of daytime sleepiness, as well as a clinical manifestation of sleep-disordered breathing.

pmc-11455326.title: 6777 Exploring the comorbidity in males with 45,X/46,XY mosaicism unveils a pattern mirroring that of Turner syndrome
pmc-11455326.creator: K Stochholm, C H Gravholt, A Berglund
pmc-11455326.description: Disclosure: K. Stochholm: None. C.H. Gravholt: None. A. Berglund: None. Background: Males with 45,X/46,XY mosaicism are rare with an apparent prevalence of 6 per 100,000 newborn males. Knowledge about associated health outcomes are limited. Females with 45,X/46,XY fall under the Turner syndrome diagnosis but males do not.

pmc-11868869.title: Rheumatoid arthritis treatment: Is exercise a game changer?
pmc-11868869.creator: Ayşegül Ketenci
pmc-11868869.description: It is known that physical activity and exercise have many effects on patients with rheumatoid arthritis, such as reducing pain, stiffness, and fatigue and having positive effects on the development of complications related to the disease. However, despite all this information, the level of exercise and physical activity in patients with rheumatoid arthritis is lower than in healthy individuals.

pmc-13312993.title: Emerging Medications in Facial Nerve Recovery: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13312993.creator: Kimberly Chan, Cheng Ma, Bao Y. Sciscent, Andreacarola Urso, Neerav Goyal, Jessyka G. Lighthall
pmc-13312993.description: ObjectiveTo systematically review the literature for medical therapies that promote facial nerve regeneration and recovery.Data SourcesPubMed/Medline, Embase, and SCOPUS databases were searched for English‐language studies published from inception through May 2025.Review MethodsHuman studies evaluating the efficacy of medical therapy on facial nerve regeneration using validated facial nerve grading scales were included.

pmc-13324149.title: Effects of zinc supplementation forms (ZnO, Zn-Lysine, Nano-ZnO) on growth performance and metabolic health in pre-weaned Holstein calves
pmc-13324149.creator: Ahmadreza Alipour, Mahdi Ganjkhanlou, Abolfazl Zali, Sadegh Hashemi, Mohammad Hasan Mortazavi, Valiollah Palangi, Wenzhu Yang, Morteza Hosseini-Ghaffari
pmc-13324149.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The pre-weaning period is critical because early-life nutrition and management influence growth, metabolic function and Rumen development, thereby affecting subsequent productivity in dairy calves. Zinc (Zn) supplementation plays a key role in supporting these processes through its involvement in enzymatic activity, antioxidant defense systems, and metabolic regulation, but conventional sources often have bioavailability limitations due to the formation of insoluble complexes in the gastrointestinal tract.

pmc-13557286.title: Classifying Foot Arch Morphologies Using High-Sensitivity Pressure Mat Technology: Prevalence Estimates and Associations With Pain, Activity Limitations, and Patient Characteristics in a Community-Based Adult Sample
pmc-13557286.creator: J. Benjamin Jackson, Harley T Davis, Rajat Das Gupta, Nathan Delahunty, Travis Dias, Heidi C Ventresca, Tyler A Gonzalez, Anthony J Alberg
pmc-13557286.description: IntroductionThere is a lack of consensus in the literature regarding the clinical understanding of foot arch contact variations in the general population, as most studies have focused on specific demographic groups or risk factors. This limits the ability of clinicians to communicate risk and interpret arch-related findings in diverse patient populations.

pmc-13679188.title: Cyanobacterial conversion of CO2 to bio-based diols and downstream valorization: biological basis, upgrading strategies, and applications
pmc-13679188.creator: Changou Pan, Han Chen, Mingyue Zhang, Shaoxiong He, Zhiqun Lin
pmc-13679188.description: Cyanobacteria have attracted growing interest as photosynthetic cell factories for the conversion of carbon dioxide (CO2) into renewable chemicals because they directly use solar energy and inorganic carbon under mild aqueous conditions. Recent advances in chassis development, genome engineering, carbon-partition control, and photobioreactor design have expanded the scope of cyanobacterial CO2-to-chemical biomanufacturing.
